learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, enabling learning new methods and theories, and providing versatility to adapt to new situations.
Knowledge of atomic structures and their defects, and the ability to control material properties by modifying atomic structures with defects.
Knowledge of the magnitudes that define the different properties characterizing the behavior of industrial materials.
Knowledge of phase diagrams, enabling fluent handling of binary equilibrium diagrams and the fundamentals of ternary diagrams.

Knowledge of the fundamentals of materials science, technology, and chemistry. Understanding the relationship between microstructure, synthesis or processing, and the properties of metallic materials.
Ability to design heat treatments to modify the microstructure and properties of steels, cast irons, and non-ferrous alloys.
Ability to use diverse materials and join them appropriately to design composite materials with controlled properties.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, and critical reasoning.
Basic knowledge of concepts related to product verification and inspection and ability to manage specifications, regulations, and mandatory standards.
Identify the structures of fundamental crystalline solids and assess the importance of different structural defects.
Interpret the different properties of materials and also be able to determine them experimentally using appropriate testing techniques.
Interpret equilibrium diagrams and use them in material development.

Fluently handle the Fe-C diagram, transformation curves, evaluate the influence of alloying elements in these products, the practical use of Jominy hardenability curves for steels, and the effects of heat treatments.
Discern the main characteristics of non-ferrous alloys of industrial interest that justify their application, assess the importance of alloying elements, and the effects of heat treatments.
Differentiate between the different families of plastic materials, ceramics, and composite materials, their main characteristics, advantages, and limitations for industrial use.
Ability to define the fundamental characteristics that describe crystalline structures.
Ability to use diffusion laws for various calculations.
Ability to determine the conventional mechanical properties of industrial materials by performing corresponding experimental tests.
Ability to determine electrical, magnetic, thermal, and optical properties using experimental methods.
Ability to interpret binary equilibrium diagrams and to place points and determine the phases present in ternary diagrams.
Ability to interpret the Fe-C diagram and the transformation curves of steels and cast irons to modify their microstructure and properties through mechanical and thermal treatments.
Ability to prepare metallographic samples, perform heat treatments, and interpret the microstructures of iron-based materials.
Ability to interpret the base equilibrium diagrams of the most important non-ferrous metallic alloys and with them define their characteristic heat treatments.
Ability to handle and interpret equilibrium diagrams in ceramic systems and to control their properties based on their manufacturing processes.
Ability to interpret the mechanical properties of plastics based on their structural characteristics and manufacturing processes.
Ability to calculate the properties of composite materials from those of their constituent simple materials.
Foster in the student a concern for the acquisition of scientific knowledge.
Lay the foundations for the student to be able to apply the acquired knowledge in engineering.
Formation of an open, critical, and entrepreneurial spirit.

syllabus_topics: Crystallography. Metallographic preparation and grain size determination.
Microstructures of steels and cast irons.

assessment_methods.method: Mandatory attendance to all practical sessions and submission of completed guides
Final exam - theory and exercises part
Non-continuous evaluation: Final exam - laboratory practices part
Non-continuous evaluation: Final exam - theory and exercises part

assessment_rules: For continuous evaluation, a minimum grade of 4 out of 10 is required on the final exam, with at least 30% of the value in each of its three parts. The overall continuous evaluation grade must be equal to or greater than 5. For non-continuous evaluation, the final exam must achieve a grade of 5 or higher, with a minimum of 30% of the value in each of its three parts. Students failing continuous assessment can resit in extraordinary calls following traditional evaluation criteria.
